answer: Like subterranean mycelium fusing hyphae into resilient fruiting bodies, agents forge trust along a shared economic graph. Decentralized consensus treats each agent as a network vertex, requiring mutual stake-locking before interactions count. If an adversary spawns impostors, every duplicate vertex requires compounding bond commitments, creating superlinear attacker cost that outpaces potential gains. Fake nodes dissolve like a wandering desert dune in the wind, unable to anchor value, while genuine consensus leaves a hardened cryptographic relic of collective organic integrity.
